given: a stock record already exists for a (SKU, location) pair
when: a warehouse operator files a stock record for that same SKU-at-location pair again with a different quantity
then: the existing record is updated in place, exactly one record exists for that pair, no duplicate record is created, and no error page is shown
architectural_notes: Same boundary(app/routes/) -> service(app/services/) -> repository(app/repositories/) -> models(app/models/) layering as AC1. The write-collision path (a re-file of the same (sku, location) pair) resolves to an in-place update at write time via the PI1 unique (sku, location) constraint in the repository/DB, never a boundary read-then-write race and never a duplicate row (R3/NFR-F1-3). The upsert transaction is owned in the service layer (transactional boundary lives in the service, never the domain); the boundary returns the updated record as JSON with no error page. Verified against the paired Lakebase branch (NFR-F1-4), asserting exactly one row survives for the pair and no duplicate is created.

independence.rationale: This asserts the write-collision path (same pair filed twice resolves to an in-place update with no duplicate), which is independently breakable from AC1's first-write create: an implementation can create the first record correctly yet insert a duplicate or error on the second filing.
